why: specify has seven mutually exclusive mode companions. Exactly one should load per invocation — that is the whole disclosure argument for this skill, and it is the largest single body reduction in the refactor (19,888 B of Standard Mode alone). An agent that loads the wrong mode acts on the wrong step sequence; one that loads all seven has paid the pre-refactor cost while looking split.
mustNotReadWhy: The six modes --extract does not select. standard-mode.md is the one that matters most: it is the default path and the largest companion, so an agent that reaches for it by habit rather than by flag is the likeliest failure here.
requiredWhy: The one mode --extract selects, plus the two shared/ companions that apply to every mode regardless of flag. The shared pair is included deliberately: they are the companions most likely to be silently dropped, because nothing in a mode's own step list forces them and an agent can produce plausible-looking output without them.
